tagline: No-code portals and internal apps on Airtable, Google Sheets, and databases.
verdictSummary: A client portal over your own Airtable base — magic-link login restricted to an allow-list, per-client filtered views, one submission form — is a real weekend build for the one portal you actually need. What doesn't come with it is Softr's actual product: a visual builder for making new portals repeatedly, a library of data-source integrations, and built-in payments and memberships.
coreLoopDIY: A client portal reading and writing through your existing Airtable base, with magic-link login restricted to an allow-list and each client seeing only rows linked to them.
whatYouLose: the visual portal builder for making new ones without code
role permissions beyond a simple client/admin flag
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay so non-engineers can launch a new portal without hiring a developer every time — that repeatability is the actual product, not any single portal.
notes: A useful example: a yes for the one portal you need right now, a kinda for the platform that lets you keep making more.
prompt:
Build one client portal — not a portal builder — backed by your existing Airtable base through its API, so records keep being edited there. Log clients in with a magic link sent to an email address that must already be on an allow-list stored in Airtable. Show each client only the records linked to them: a list view with a configurable set of visible columns, and a detail view per record. Add one submission form that appends a new row to a chosen table, with file uploads passed straight through to Airtable's own attachment fields. Give client records a simple role flag distinguishing an ordinary client from an admin who sees everything. Cache Airtable reads briefly to stay comfortably under its rate limits.

Do not build a drag-and-drop page builder, payments, or memberships — pages are defined in a config file, and that's the honest builder here. This makes one portal well; making another one means writing more config, not clicking through a visual tool.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Softr portal?
faq.a: The underlying data, yes, if it's already in Airtable or a similar source — this build reads from the same kind of data source directly. The page layouts and Softr's own blocks need to be rebuilt as config here.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: As a responsive web page, yes — client-facing portals like this are usually simple enough to work fine on a phone browser.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting, typically a few dollars a month, plus whatever your Airtable plan already costs — no separate per-user portal fee.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Making the next portal quickly. Softr's visual builder lets you spin up a new client portal in an afternoon without touching code; here, every new portal is a small development project, even a fast one.
